newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris see new oil deal with Russia's LUKoil.
newsitem.headline: Azeris see new oil deal with Russia's LUKoil.

text.p: Azerbaijan and Russian oil giant LUKoil will sign a deal this week on joint development of the Yalama oilfield in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea, the presidential press service said on Tuesday.
It quoted Azeri President Haydar Aliyev as saying the agreement would be formalised when Aliyev pays an official visit to Moscow on July 3-4.
LUKoil president Vagit Alekperov said in Baku in May that the offshore field, about 200 km north of Baku in the Caspian, is estimated to contain at least 50 million tonnes of oil.

Yalama is near the limit of what Azerbaijan considers its territorial sector of the Caspian. The sea's status is the subject of a dispute between its five littoral states, but Azerbaijan, one of the states, has pushed ahead with major energy investment deals.
LUKoil already has stakes in three other joint projects with Azeri state oil firm SOCAR to develop Caspian fields.
Russia's largest oil producer is also negotiating on joint development of the Inam field, 120 km southeast of Baku and estimated to contain about 200 million tonnes of crude.
Azerbaijan has already signed more than $18 billion in contracts with foreign firms to develop its huge untapped offshore energy reserves.
